devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four words. After everything that has happened, God says it plainly one more time.

There is a mercy in this repetition. God knows what we are prone to, and He does not assume we learned the lesson the first time. He says it again.

Modern readers can feel exempt here. Most of us have never carved a statue. But an idol is simply anything that takes the place God alone should occupy — anything we look to for the security, identity, meaning or happiness that only He can give.

Idols are usually good things that have become ultimate things. Family is good; family as your source of identity is an idol. Work is good; work as your source of worth is an idol. Money, approval, health, comfort, even ministry — all good gifts, all capable of quietly taking God's throne.

Here is a useful test: what would devastate you most to lose? What do you think about when you have nothing else to think about? What do you pursue without ever deciding to?

John ends his letter with the same brevity: "Dear children, keep yourselves from idols" (1 John 5:21). It is the last line of the letter — the thing he most wanted them to remember.

Christ has not left us to manage this alone. His Spirit reshapes our desires from the inside.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What would devastate you most to lose?
2. What good thing in your life may have become an ultimate thing?
3. What would it look like to hand that back to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, search my heart and show me my idols. Take Your rightful place at the centre of my life. Amen.
